findings.text: The first paragraph does its job. A newcomer learns what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves before anything else on the page.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: This is Athena's home URL, but the title is about a different project that the newcomer has never heard of. Someone arriving to learn about Athena may think they are on the wrong page before they reach the opening paragraph.
findings.source: Title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The opening says Athena's main job is turning a one-line request into a traceable commit, with its cost and verdict. The page never shows that. It shows a different skill, reading another project, so the newcomer sees no example of the main product: no commit, no cost record, no checker's verdict.
findings.source: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it"

findings.text: The next step is concrete: clone, run setup.sh, try one command. But the newcomer is not told about supported operating systems, the account or API key that Claude Code needs, or what a typical run costs, even though the page says Athena "records what each step cost."
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: A link near the top jumps straight to Next steps, so the newcomer does not have to scroll past the whole study. That helps.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" (header)

findings.text: This link appears in the header with no explanation. A newcomer is not the owner and cannot tell what these proposals are or whether they should care.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed state machine of firstmate, with exit codes, place counters and twelve transition cards. This is far more than a newcomer needs and hides the short Athena pitch and the next steps around it.
findings.source: Headings "Transitions", "Counters" and cards t1–t12, e.g. "the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued"

findings.text: The same facts are stated four or five times, so the page is longer and harder to skim. Sentences such as "The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it" read like internal audit notes, not explanation.
findings.source: Yolo and place rules repeated under "Words used first", "What firstmate is", "One piece of work", "When things go wrong", the t3/t4/t10 cards, "Why it is built this way" and the Glossary

findings.text: For a reader who does want to know firstmate, the Start here section works well. It defines terms before using them, follows one task from start to finish, and lists failure cases plainly.

The page is honest that nothing was run and every claim comes from reading the source. This supports its traceability pitch, and each bracketed claim id links to the exact file and lines at the pinned commit.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read"

findings.text: This refers to a folder in a repository the newcomer has not seen. It means nothing to them.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
